witness_description: Conflict graph G = K2 (2 passengers, single edge {0,1}), per-trip passenger capacity c = 1 (boat capacity k = c+1 = 2 including Charon). The ferry instance is feasible with capacity 1: Charon carries passenger 0 across (passenger 1 left alone, independent), returns empty (passenger 0 alone on the right, independent), then carries passenger 1 across. Yet G = K2 is not 1-colorable: the two passengers cannot be partitioned into 1 independent set since they are adjacent.
refutation_explanation: The quoted sentence infers, from the boat carrying at most c passengers per trip, that the passengers can be partitioned into at most c independent sets (a c-coloring of G). Read as an implication -- feasibility with capacity c implies chi(G) <= c -- it is false: with c = 1 and G = K2 the instance is solvable (Charon shuttles the two conflicting passengers one at a time, and whenever he is absent from a bank that bank holds a single passenger, trivially independent), but chi(K2) = 2 > 1, so no partition into at most c = 1 independent sets exists. Transport capacity bounds how many passengers cross per trip, not how the conflict graph colors; nothing forces the sets carried (or left behind) to assemble into c independent classes. The classic wolf-goat-cabbage instance (path P3, c = 1, chi = 2) is a further witness in the same swept space.
search_space: All labeled conflict graphs on n = 1..4 vertices (every subset of the C(n,2) possible edges, lexicographic mask order) crossed with every capacity c = 1..n-1. Ferry feasibility decided exactly by BFS over the full configuration space (subset of passengers on the left bank x Charon's side, <= 2^n * 2 states; moves = Charon plus any subset of at most c passengers from his bank, with the unattended bank required independent). c-colorability decided exactly by enumerating all c^n color assignments. Integer/frozenset arithmetic only; deterministic fixed iteration order; first witness in that order reported and re-verified by assertion.
